headline: Rwanda Celebrates 22 New Baby Mountain Gorillas
meta_description: Rwanda named 22 baby mountain gorillas at an annual conservation ceremony as the Virunga Massif population more than doubles since the 1980s.
summary_short: Rwanda celebrated 22 newborn mountain gorillas at its annual naming ceremony, marking a major milestone for the species in the Virunga Massif.
body:
Rwanda has named 22 baby mountain gorillas at its annual conservation ceremony, underscoring one of Africa's most remarkable wildlife recoveries. The population in the Virunga Massif has surged from roughly 250 individuals in the early 1980s to more than 600 today.

The naming ceremony represents far more than a symbolic gesture. Each newborn gorilla represents years of dedicated protection and habitat management by Rwandan conservationists, park rangers, and international partners working together to shield these critically endangered animals from poaching and habitat loss.

The dramatic population increase—more than doubling over four decades—stands as powerful evidence that focused, sustained conservation effort works. The Virunga Massif, a volcanic mountain range spanning Rwanda, Uganda, and the Democratic Republic of Congo, remains one of the last refuges for these magnificent primates.
quick_facts: 22 baby mountain gorillas named at Rwanda's annual ceremony
Virunga Massif population grew from ~250 in early 1980s to 600+
Rwanda leads mountain gorilla conservation in volcanic Virunga region
